title: OpenAI models find OpenBSD System V semaphore context-switch use-after-free
summary: A semaphore object could be freed while a thread slept in sys_semget(), leaving the resumed context with a stale pointer. OpenAI says researchers reproduced the kernel use-after-free and confirmed local privilege-escalation potential.
ai_role: OpenAI states its models identified this 23-year-old issue; OpenAI researchers reproduced it. The public OpenBSD fix commit describes the context-switch use-after-free in sys_semget().
classification_note: The public OpenBSD fix commit is dated 2026-05-22; OpenAI publicly attributed the model-assisted finding on 2026-06-22. This chronology does not establish when defenders first knew of it.
remediation_note: OpenBSD’s public fix commit is dated 2026-05-22, before OpenAI’s June 22 public attribution. No CVE is listed in the cited sources.

impacts.conditions: The OpenBSD commit identifies a use-after-free after tsleep during System V semaphore context-switch handling. This records the memory-safety defect only; the source does not establish a downstream consequence.
impacts.exploitation: Exploitation in the wild is not established by the cited source.
